workflow_scorecard.change: Eight resident task-agent slots and V2 recycling
workflow_scorecard.evidence: Eleven distinct task-agent threads ran with no thread-limit error. Active concurrency averaged 1.432 and reached four; the predecessor averaged 1.121 and reached three.
workflow_scorecard.interpretation: The larger resident pool and automatic recycling removed the previous slot deadlock. The different runnable graph prevents attributing all concurrency gain to the capacity change.

workflow_scorecard.change: 1.10 GiB hard memory floor; 1.50 GiB warning
workflow_scorecard.evidence: Twenty heavy admissions occurred below the old 1.50 GiB floor, while 26 resource samples were denied under the current rules.
workflow_scorecard.interpretation: The new threshold admitted useful work under warnings while still failing closed below the hard floor. This is the clearest direct success from PR #98.

workflow_scorecard.evidence: The 129 transcript-classified dotnet command families had a maximum overlap of one.
workflow_scorecard.interpretation: The machine discipline held throughout repeated build and test cycles.

workflow_scorecard.change: Retention reason, release trigger, V2 follow-up lifecycle
workflow_scorecard.evidence: Only 11 threads handled 106 turns, compared with 27 threads and 70 turns in the predecessor. One reused Sol/high completion thread alone consumed 134.0M tokens and about $69.05.
workflow_scorecard.interpretation: Reuse solved slot churn and preserved live-debugging context, but the completion role grew across implementation, CI diagnosis, production dispatch, and reconciliation. Add a role-change or context-cost release trigger.

workflow_scorecard.evidence: Sol/high was used for bounded prompt and completion work, while independent specification reviews remained Sol/xhigh. Review agents returned 8 finding verdicts and 5 accept-with-fixes verdicts before 11 clean acceptances.
workflow_scorecard.interpretation: The allocation rule preserved strong independent review, but the long-lived completion thread was no longer a bounded deterministic role.

workflow_scorecard.evidence: The root patched state.md 207 times, or 18.51 times per effective hour, versus 10.19 in the predecessor.
workflow_scorecard.interpretation: Urgent re-freezes created real transitions, but the ledger still became a high-frequency operational log. Coalesce resource and gate updates more aggressively.

workflow_scorecard.evidence: Four markers clearly announced production recovery, two live-drift correction waves, and maintenance work.
workflow_scorecard.interpretation: The markers were useful milestone boundaries. The workflow text calls for the marker before the first implementation writer, so repeated use should be explicitly allowed only for material re-freezes.

workflow_scorecard.evidence: Eighteen scoped commits reached canonical main and nine source-session CI runs completed without a push-approval pause; eight CI runs succeeded and the one failed run was corrected at a later exact SHA.
workflow_scorecard.interpretation: Publication no longer interrupted the recovery loop. Two production-write approval waits remained because paid generation and Kicktipp mutation are outside that Git/GitHub authority envelope.

limitations: The Astra-versus-Sol counterfactual reprices the exact same observed token mix. It does not estimate how Sol/xhigh would have changed decisions, latency, retries, or token consumption.
The comparison session had a different ready graph and objective. Concurrency and delivery differences are evidence about this run, not a controlled experiment for PR #98.
API list-price equivalents are a common cost unit; Codex subscription quota and billing are separate and cannot be reconstructed from transcript token counters.
Tool timing is transcript timing around tool calls. It measures orchestration-visible occupancy rather than CPU time.
The final P1-04/P1-05 commits document plans only. Those tasks were not implemented in this session.
